name: UK Community Tree Planting Programme
summary: Pays for community woodland and hedge planting of native trees on publicly accessible land in the UK, with trees, advice and two years of aftercare payments.
reporting: Partners must provide accurate information about the progress of their project and be open about any challenges experienced.

eligibility.rule: Have a community base or social benefit
Have a bank account in the applicant organisation's name
Have signed landowner or manager permission covering legal requirements
Plant trees in public or publicly-accessible spaces
Plant indigenous tree species with stated appropriate exceptions
Engage community members in tree planting and enjoying woodland benefits
Have clear plans for maintenance and sustainability
Plant 100–10,000 trees a year. The grant covers up to £2.15 per tree including protection and mulch

All fully completed eligible applications will be assessed by a grants panel.

eligibility.quote: Your organisation must be community-based and/or have a social benefit e.g. a school, community group, social enterprise, non-governmental organisation, parish council, etc.
You must have a bank account in the name of the applicant organisation
You must have signed permission from the owner or manager of the land indicating that the project meets all legal requirements
Plant trees in public/publicly-accessible spaces: sites that are accessible to the public, including schools, parks, rights of way, and sites managed by community groups
Plant indigenous tree species. This may include traditional fruit trees and 'honorary natives' where appropriate
Engage community members in tree planting and enjoying the benefits of woodlands
Have clear plans for maintenance and sustainability
Projects to range from 100 – 10,000 trees planted per year, with a maximum price equivalent to £2.15/tree (inclusive of tree protection and mulch).
